summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Plant tissue culture exploits cellular totipotency to regenerate whole plants from excised explants under aseptic nutrient conditions. Micropropagation enables rapid commercial cloning of thousands of genetically identical somaclones.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 4.1 Fundamentals of Plant Tissue Culture
- **Cellular Totipotency**: Conceived by **Gottlieb Haberlandt (1902)**, totipotency is the inherent genetic and physiological capacity of a living, nucleated plant cell or tissue fragment (**Explant**) to divide, redifferentiate, and regenerate into an entire, mature adult plant.
- **Explant**: Any excised piece of plant tissue (*shoot tip, leaf disc, stem segment, hypocotyl, anther, embryo*) surface-sterilized and inoculated onto a sterile synthetic nutrient medium.
- **Nutrient Medium Composition (MS Medium - Murashige & Skoog)**:
  1. **Carbon / Energy Source**: Sucrose ($2\text{--}3\%$) is mandatory because cultured cells lack active photosynthetic autotrophy.
  2. **Inorganic Macronutrients & Micronutrients**: Nitrogen ($\text{NH}_4^+, \text{NO}_3^-$), Phosphorus, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Iron, Zinc, Boron.
  3. **Vitamins & Amino Acids**: Thiamine (Vitamin $\text{B}_1$), Nicotinic acid, Pyridoxine, Inositol, and Glycine.
  4. **Phytohormones (Growth Regulators)**:
     - **Auxin (NAA, 2,4-D, IAA)**: Induces cell division and initiates root formation (**Rhizogenesis**).
     - **Cytokinin (BAP, Kinetin, Zeatin)**: Stimulates cell division and shoot bud differentiation (**Caulogenesis**).
     - **High Auxin : Low Cytokinin** $\implies$ Root induction.
     - **Low Auxin : High Cytokinin** $\implies$ Shoot induction.
     - **Balanced Auxin : Cytokinin** $\implies$ Unorganized proliferating cell mass called **Callus**.

### 4.2 Micropropagation & Somaclones
- **Micropropagation**: The rapid *in-vitro* asexual multiplication of plants using tissue culture techniques within minimal space and time.
- **Somaclones**: All plantlets produced via micropropagation are genetically identical to each other and to the parent mother plant (clones).
- **Commercial Application**: Widely utilized for commercial propagation of high-value crops including **Tomato, Banana, Apple, Orchids, Sugarcane, and Strawberry**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Somaclonal Variation
conceptBreakdown.title: Somaclonal Variation
conceptBreakdown.content: Genetic and epigenetic variations that arise during prolonged in-vitro callus culture are termed somaclonal variations, which can occasionally yield useful agronomic mutants displaying enhanced drought tolerance or disease resistance.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Synthetic Seeds (Synseeds)
conceptBreakdown.title: Synthetic Seeds (Synseeds)
conceptBreakdown.content: Somatic embryos induced from callus are encapsulated within calcium alginate hydrogel beads containing nutrients, fungicides, and bio-fertilizers to produce synthetic artificial seeds for field sowing.
